## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: the new `CRITERION_HINT` tells users to leave out "shall", but under the supported `require_shall=True` option the validator rejects every criterion that lacks " shall ". This review read `app/criteria.py` and `tests/test_criteria.py` in full and checked them against `config.example.yml`. It did not run the tests. The new `BULLET_HINT` matches the `text.startswith("- ")` check at `app/criteria.py:5`.

## Changes
The pull request rewords `CRITERION_HINT` so it asks for direct action bullets without "shall", and rewords `BULLET_HINT` to show the exact `- ` prefix. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` at the repository root, which the pull-request body does not mention.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/criteria.py:1 — correctness — Hint forbids "shall" that require_shall=True needs — With `require_shall=True`, a criterion written as the hint says, such as `- Save the result`, is rejected because `accepts_criterion` returns `" shall " in text` (`app/criteria.py:7-8`), and `tests/test_criteria.py:20-21` asserts that rejection. `CRITERION_HINT` is a single static string with no per-mode variant. Projects that set the `require_shall` option from `config.example.yml:1` therefore get a hint whose advice always fails validation. — Users in `require_shall` mode who follow the hint have every criterion rejected and get no correct guidance on how to fix it. — Fix: Keep the hint neutral about "shall", or add a separate hint for `require_shall=True` that tells users to include "shall" and choose between the two hints based on the option.
